items.followUp: What is software piracy? Explain any two types of software piracy.

rubric.why: The definition must identify software piracy as unauthorized use, copying, or distribution of software.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that software is used, copied, or distributed without authorization.

rubric.why: Softlifting means making unauthorized copies or using software on more computers than the licence allows.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming and correctly explaining this type.

rubric.why: Counterfeiting involves illegally duplicating software and presenting or selling it as genuine.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming and correctly explaining this type.

rubric.why: Online piracy is the illegal downloading or sharing of software through the internet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming and correctly explaining this type.

modelAnswer: Software piracy is the unauthorized copying, use, or distribution of copyrighted software.
Three types of software piracy are:
Softlifting: making unauthorized copies of software for use on more computers than the licence permits.
Counterfeiting: illegally copying and selling software as if it were genuine.
Online piracy: illegally downloading or sharing software through the internet.

items.followUp: Write any two disadvantages of using a flowchart.

rubric.why: Preparing a flowchart can take considerable time.
rubric.description: States that drawing a flowchart is time-consuming.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this disadvantage or another valid one.

rubric.why: Flowcharts for large problems may become complex and difficult to modify.
rubric.description: States that a flowchart can become complex or difficult to modify.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this or another distinct valid disadvantage.

modelAnswer: Drawing a flowchart can be time consuming.
A flowchart for a large problem can become complex and difficult to modify.
